items.quote: on a large base of about 1 lakh plus direct and indirect distribution that we do on fans, we would have added about 3,000 to 4,000 more outlets.

items.statement: NIM expected to decline to 8.35% in H2 FY27 due to repo rate hike impact.
items.quote: So we feel the margin would come down to around 8.35% for the second half of the year.

items.statement: Micro banking loan growth guidance for FY27 maintained at 12-14%.
items.quote: It would be somewhere between 12% to 14%, in between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Secured book target 56% by end of FY27, improving 5% annually thereafter.
items.quote: Today, it is at 52%. We expect it to reach 56% by end of the year. And going forward every year 5% improvement.

items.statement: Opex to ATA ratio expected at 6.2% for FY27, 20 bps lower than earlier guidance.
items.quote: Now considering the way it is moving, we feel it may end up at 6.2%. So there could be a saving of 0.2 opex to ATA ratio.

items.statement: Credit cost for H2 FY27 expected similar to H1, within guided range.
items.quote: As we said, credit cost in H2 is similar to the credit cost in H1.

items.statement: ROA likely to overshoot upper end of guided range for FY27.
items.quote: So summing up, it looks like a high probability of a significant beat on the upper end at our ROA.

items.statement: Raising INR409 crores equity from QIBs via preferential allotment; balance from INR2,000 crores resolution by July 2027.
items.quote: We propose to raise equity capital of INR409 crores from QIBs by issuing shares on a preferential basis to marquee investors, International Finance Corporation, Bajaj Life Insurance, HDFC Life Insurance, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Cost of funds expected to increase by 10 bps due to repo rate hike.
items.quote: And as you rightly mentioned, repo rate has gone up by 25 bps. So that will have an impact of around 10 bps on the margin.

items.statement: Calibrated rate revisions on retail TD and SA planned as deposits churn.
items.quote: We have a calibrated rate revision we'll do as we go along. As of now, we have not done anything, okay? But yes, as we go along, we do some changes in retail TD rate or SA rate.

items.statement: Microfinance demand increased, but cautious approach in some states; growth calibrated at 12-14%.
items.quote: So you are right, the demand has increased, especially from the last quarter of the last financial year. And among repeat also, we are seeing a good demand. But at the same time, as I mentioned, in some of the states, we need to be cautious, careful and carefully choose location where we want to disburse loans in this

items.statement: Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra poses limited risk; exposure to eligible agri loans is small.
items.quote: As far as Karnataka and Maharashtra is concerned, these remain in our key watch list following the recent government and SLBC announcement, which could affect collection to some extent mainly because of government interventions. However, the guidelines primarily apply to pure agri portfolio, while our exposure is large

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper on insurance commissions could impact income; awaiting final guidelines.
items.quote: IRDAI's notification is a consultation paper, and we await the final guidelines on the matter. We remain engaged with our insurance partners as well as through IBA channels. Since discussions with IRDAI are ongoing and submissions are due on October 25, it would be premature to elaborate further.

items.statement: MD succession process expected to complete in 3-4 months from September 1.
items.quote: And we hope to complete the process in around 3 to 4 months, starting September 1. So we should be able to complete it in 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: Expects FY27 EBITDA margin around 12% plus/minus, with improvement starting next year.
items.quote: So I think this year, we will be at similar kind of EBITDA of around 12% plus/minus. That is what for this year is our take.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth expected mid-teen to slightly high-teen.
items.quote: But I think our initial assessment of 12%, 14%, I think we should do a between mid-teen to a little high-teen numbers for the year-end.

items.statement: Targets exports to be at least 30% plus of overall revenue by end of this year.
items.quote: So our first target, I think by the end of this year should be that at least 30% plus of our revenue should come from export and we have been working towards that.

items.statement: Remaining H2 FY27 capex of Rs 50-75 crore; no significant capex next year.
items.value: Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 70 crore, Rs. 75 crore
items.quote: I think we'll have another about between Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 70 crore, Rs. 75 crore of spend that will happen in the second half. And then I think nothing beyond that.

items.statement: New ethoxylation facility to reach peak utilization by end of FY28, targeting 3x capex as peak sales.
items.quote: So probably we'll have the peak utilization targets by end of FY28. And we still stick to the target of 3x of the CAPEX value to be the peak sales revenue.

items.statement: Reliance EO expansion expected in Q1 next financial year, enabling higher EO allocation.
items.quote: So we are expecting in the first quarter of next financial year for the Reliance expansion to kick in, and we should get higher amount of EO allocation from the first quarter

items.statement: Freight costs doubled/tripled YoY, compressing core B2B EBITDA margin; not all customers absorb increases.
items.quote: Even though our exports have grown significantly, the freight costs have almost doubled, tripled over what they were in the first half of last year or Q2 of last year. That has significantly impacted our EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Pharma, aroma segments to drive steady gross margin improvement once they scale, a few quarters away.
items.quote: as these segments like pharma, aroma, you know, start becoming a significant part of the overall business, we should see steady gross margin improvement, you know, going forward.

items.statement: Focus on higher-margin products; tail-cutting bottom 5% low-margin products improved gross and EBITDA margins.
items.quote: Tail cutting means with the bottom 5% of the products who have the least margins are cut off from the tail and we stop producing or selling those products.

items.statement: AHN Q2 is seasonally weakest; Q3 and Q4 will be peak season for Animal Health.
items.quote: Generally, the second quarter is the weakest for the AHN division. The third and fourth quarters will peak.

items.statement: B2C/institutional business targeted EBITDA positive in H2 and breakeven for full year.
items.quote: So our aim is that at least in the next two quarters, at least H2 should also be an EBITDA positive second half for us. And overall, on a full year basis, we should at least breakeven in this business

items.statement: All cash flows to go into debt reduction; working capital debt-free by mid next year.
items.quote: But yes, currently, all cash flows will go into debt reduction.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia greenfield project: land lease approved, next steps and timelines in 8-12 months.
items.quote: Hopefully some of these developments will happen over the next 8 months to 12 months.

items.statement: FY27 disbursements to surpass last year's INR35,000 crore; guidance intact.
items.quote: the guidance that we have given is that, in FY27 also, we will surpass disbursement that we did last FY, and that guidance remains intact.

items.statement: AUM target of near INR5 lakh crore by end of FY27; may be 1,000-2,000 crore short.
items.quote: we stand by the target of reaching near about INR5,00,000 crores, maybe more than that, maybe 1,000 or 2,000 possible shortfall but the target is fully intact for end of FY27.

items.statement: H2 FY26 expected to replicate H1 performance; AUM to exceed last year.
items.quote: the numbers that we have shown in H1 will be kind of replica of what is going to be in H2.

items.statement: Railway pipeline over INR20 lakh crore across DFC, high-speed rail, and freight lines.
items.quote: So overall, pie that comes out to be more than INR20 lakh crores.

items.statement: From FY28, minimum INR50,000 crore annual disbursement from Indian Railways for a decade.
items.quote: That pie will be going forward, maybe from FY28 onwards for next decade, minimum 50,000 crores every year coming from the Indian Railways.

items.statement: H2 lending pipeline includes metros, ports, renewables, thermal, Gencos, and road linkages.
items.quote: Next, in H2, you will find that we will be lending to metros, ports, renewable energy, thermal power, Gencos that have linkages with the Railways. We will be lending to few road linkages also.

items.statement: Non-railway margins 2-3.5x higher than railway 35 bps; PAT to grow despite flat AUM.
items.quote: whatever assets we are replacing was of 35 bps and whatever assets adding is more than 100 bps.

items.statement: Minimum margin of INR0.85-0.90 per unit targeted on diversified loans.
items.quote: In every scenario, strategy we have followed is that we must make at least a margin of INR0.90 or INR0.85 minimum.

items.statement: WACC of 6.55% to be maintained despite rate hardening; hedging cost below 6.3%.
items.quote: we are maintaining country-best WACC, weighted average cost of capital, that is 6.55% that we did last year. This year also, we hope to maintain that despite of the hardening of the rates.

items.statement: No prepayment penalty and no floor price offered to borrowers; positions as cheapest lender.
items.quote: Number one, there is no prepayment penalty. Listen to it very carefully. My first proposition to all my prospective borrowers that, we are not putting any prepayment penalty

items.statement: Target mix by 2030: 60% pure Railways, 40% diversification.
items.quote: Given the way we have forecasted that by 2030, our mix will be 60% pure Railways and 40% will be diversification

items.statement: Reducing WACC by increasing share of 54EC bonds and ECB borrowings.
items.quote: We are very actively looking at reducing our WACC by increasing the share of 54EC bonds and also ECB, so that borrowing costs are least cost amongst other NBFCs

items.statement: No prepayment pressure; prepayments from others are business opportunities for IRFC.
items.quote: So, I'm perhaps the only NBFC in the country who is not having this pressure, and there is a reason behind this.

items.statement: Bank of America to acquire 49.9% stake in Jio Credit, bringing around Rs. 18,000 crore growth capital.
items.quote: In our lending vertical, we struck a landmark partnership during the quarter with Bank of America agreeing to acquire a 49.9% stake in Jio Credit. The transaction, which is subject to regulatory approvals, is expected to bring around Rs. 18,000 crore in growth capital.

items.statement: First tranche of about Rs. 9,500 crore from Bank of America into Jio Credit, subject to approvals.
items.quote: The infusion of the first tranche of its investment of around Rs. 9,500 crore from Bank of America into Jio Credit Limited, subject to regulatory and statutory approvals, will further bolster our capital base and strengthen our balance sheet for long-term expansion.

items.statement: Deliberate pivot to margin-accretive merchant segments; let go of high-volume, low-margin engagements.
items.quote: Consequently, we chose to let go of certain high-volume, low-margin engagements, as our focus remains firmly on profitable growth rather than volume expansion alone.

items.statement: Net processing margin rose to 14 bps in Q2 FY27 from 9 bps a year ago and 12 bps in Q1.
items.quote: Our net processing margin increased to 14 basis points in Q2 FY27, up from 9 basis points in Q2 FY26 and 12 basis points in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing stable at 7.08% in Q2 FY27 versus 7.07% in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Our average cost of borrowing, excluding TREPS, stood at 7.08% in Q2 FY27, compared to 7.07% in Q1 FY27, demonstrating strong stability in a dynamic interest rate environment.

items.statement: Over 70% of AUM on floating rates, allowing rate changes to pass to borrowers with minimal lag.
items.quote: On interest rate risk management, over 70% of our Assets Under Management are on floating rates, enabling interest rate adjustments to be seamlessly passed on to borrowers with minimal time lag.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank received approvals to launch 3-in-1 savings account and act as Banker to the Issue.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also received key regulatory approvals to launch our 3-in-1 Savings Account as well as to act as ‘Banker to the Issue’ for public offerings, including IPOs, which will open up new revenue streams for the payments bank.

items.statement: Jio Credit book mix: mortgages 44.5%, corporate and SME 44.2%, retail LAS 11.3%.
items.quote: Mortgages, comprising Home Loans and Loan Against Property, account for 44.5% of the total portfolio, with an average ticket size of Rs. 1.4 crore and an average tenor of 15.9 years.

items.statement: IRDAI draft insurance distribution regulations may reshape industry and lead to consolidation; JFS will recalibrate strategy.
items.quote: We view this as a significant regulatory shift that will reshape the industry landscape and may lead to consolidation.

items.statement: Jio Allianz General Insurance in advanced stages of securing regulatory approvals to commence operations.
items.quote: In general and health insurance, Jio Allianz General Insurance Limited is in advanced stages for securing regulatory approvals to commence operations.

items.statement: GIFT City entity received IFSCA approval to launch BlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund, planned this quarter.
items.quote: Finally, another important milestone during the quarter was our GIFT City entity receiving regulatory approval from the IFSCA to launch the BlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund. The fund planned for launch during the current quarter, opens up global investment pipelines for Indian investors.

items.statement: Reinsurance GWP moderated sequentially as primary insurers recalibrated crop insurance exposure to seasonal factors.
items.quote: Primary insurance carriers recalibrated their exposure to crop insurance to align with seasonal and environmental factors, which moderated sequential volume.

items.statement: JioBlackRock AMC partnered with over 15,000 MF and SIF distributors and launched Regular Plans across offerings.
items.quote: As highlighted in our distribution strategy, we have now partnered with over 15,000 Mutual Fund and Specialized Investment Fund distributors, and have launched Regular Plans across all our product offerings to complement our Direct Plans.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank expanded toll operations to 20 national highway toll plazas and 2 MLFF plazas.
items.quote: During the quarter, we expanded our toll operations footprint, which is now operational across 20 national highway toll plazas as well as 2 Multi-Lane Free-Flow barrierless toll plazas.

items.statement: Maintains AUM growth guidance of 20-25% for the year despite flat gold prices.
items.quote: We will continue to give the same guidance in spite of the gold prices being almost flat. So we will give a AUM growth of about 20% to 25% for the year.

items.statement: Targets 3% ROA and 18% ROE, with potential upside to prior guidance.
items.quote: Our target ROA we are trying to reach is 3% and correspondingly try and touch an 18% ROE.

items.statement: Plans to add at least 150 gold loan branches in H2 FY27.
items.quote: In addition to the 74 branches we added in quarter 2, we propose to add at least another 150 branches in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Expects stronger H2 performance due to seasonality and branch additions.
items.quote: Historically, the second half of the year is a much stronger period for us, which is giving us confidence that in spite of the headwinds you mentioned, we would be able to perform to our guidance, which we have been giving in the earlier quarters for this year on AUM growth.

items.statement: Small ticket LAP disbursements to pick up in Q3 and Q4, with better yields.
items.quote: The pickup has not been that great, but it will definitely pick up in Q3, and you will see further better yields as well as the ticket sizes the normalized range.

items.statement: Yield on core loan book stable at 16.40% in Q2.
items.quote: Our overall yield on the core loan book remained constant in quarter 2 compared to quarter 1 at 16.40 levels.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing flat at 7.80% for Q2 and previous three quarters.
items.quote: On the cost of borrowing, in spite of headwinds, we were able to keep our weighted average cost of borrowing for quarter 2, flat at the same level as the previous 3 quarters at 7.80.

items.statement: Gold loan Stage II and III increases are technical due to customer behavior change, not credit risk.
items.quote: The increase in Stage II from 2.7% to 3.6% and in Stage III from 1.6% to 1.8% are entirely on account of this changed construct in gold loans. We are sufficiently collateralized and do not see these optical indicators as indicating any enhanced risk on the portfolio.

items.statement: AUM per gold branch increased from INR8 crores to INR16 crores, improving operating leverage.
items.quote: If you see my trajectory on the AUM per gold branch, it has moved from INR8 crores per branch to INR16 crores per branch.

items.statement: Insurance income contributes about 0.1% to ROA.
items.quote: So, from an ROA tree perspective, I would put the number at about 0.1% in the ROA tree from an income perspective, a little over 0.1%.

items.statement: New gold branches typically turn profitable in 12-13 months at INR6-7 crores AUM.
items.quote: Typically, a branch, if it reaches about INR6 crores to INR7 crores of AUM, it turns profitable for us. when the price is going on an upward trajectory or even the price that is there today, in 12 to 13 months, the branch starts touching that number.

items.statement: Approval rates for ST LAP improved from 30% to mid-40% levels.
items.quote: So approval rates for earlier when we were coming out of the woods had dropped down to about 30% levels. Now steadily, they have moved up to the mid-40% or the early 40% levels.

items.statement: Medium ticket LAP yields stable at 11.5-12.5%.
items.quote: We hold a yield of about 11.5% to 12.5% in that business.

items.statement: Expects Q3 and Q4 volumes stronger than Q2; H2 typically 20% higher than H1.
items.quote: Based on our current indication, we expect Q3 and Q4 volumes to be stronger than Q2. Overall volumes and historically also H2 is always 20% up on H1.

items.statement: Exports expected to be 45% higher this year than previous year.
items.quote: Year-on-year, we expect this year to be 45% higher than our previous year.

items.statement: Seamless tube facility production trials planned for February or March 2027.
items.quote: The sizing mill and straightening mills have been received and installed, and we plan to undertake production trials in February or March of 2027.

items.statement: Total seamless tube capex budget INR170 crores; INR120 crores spent as of Q2.
items.quote: the total budgeted cost is approximately INR170 crores, okay? Out of this is funded by INR110 crores via term loan. The rest is from internal accruals, okay?

items.statement: Plans INR60 crores immediate capex via warrants and pref shares over next two quarters.
items.quote: close to INR60 crores we are planning on an immediate capex via warrants and pref shares, which we would be spending between the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Further INR50 crores capex on seamless tube in H2; total H2 capex about INR110 crores.
items.quote: we are looking at a further balanced capex of close to INR50-odd crores out of the INR170 crores, which is there.

items.statement: Backward integration into seamless tubes expected to add 3-4% margin on overall business.
items.quote: on the overall business, we should be having a margin of approximately 3% to 4% once we use our own seamless tubes for it.

items.statement: Seamless tube cost expected 8-10% lower than existing buying prices.
items.quote: it should be at around approximately 8% to 10% lesser than -- or you could say more competitive than existing buying prices.

items.statement: Price revisions with OEMs and Tier 1 customers to support Q3 and Q4.
items.quote: the price revisions, including -- concluded with the OEMs and Tier 1 customers are expected to support us during the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Steel prices increasing each quarter; OEMs and mills discussing another increase in Q3.
items.quote: steel as a commodity, we see increase going on in each and every quarter. I do believe that OEMs and mills are also talking about another increase in quarter 3 as well.

items.statement: Agri segment momentum to continue in Q3; tractor production planned at 13,000-14,000 in Oct-Nov.
items.quote: We expect this momentum to continue into Q3, supported by relatively lower inventory levels of tractors in the market.

items.statement: Extruded axle beam production at 80% of current output; to reach 100% by Q3 or Q4.
items.quote: Commercial production of our extruded axle beam has commenced and the capacity utilization of this is approximately 80% of our current output.

items.statement: Preferential issue of INR63.6 crores to fund expansion initiatives.
items.quote: The company is completely focused on capacity expansion and gearing up for the coming years, which is also witnessed by a preferential issue to the tune of INR63.6 crores.

items.statement: Difficult to guide on return to 14-15% EBITDA margins due to cost escalation and settlement pressures.
items.quote: Yes, it is difficult currently. The companies are facing a lot of pressures in terms of escalation and then the settlements and everything.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 guidance of double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-teens EBITDA growth, with H2 high-teens growth.
items.quote: We had given guidance of double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-teens EBITDA growth in FY27. In H1, as you know, we have already significantly overachieved relative to that run rate.

items.statement: Expects high-teens EBITDA growth for H2 FY27.
items.quote: High teens is for H2. The number that I'm talking about is high teens growth is specifically for H2, okay?

items.statement: Expects double-digit RevPAR growth in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: So we are very much on track for double-digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well.

items.statement: Capex for five owned pipeline projects is INR 1,432 crores; INR 150 crores spent, INR 450 crores by year-end, INR 600 crores next year.
items.quote: So, I'll tell you the capex for our five contracted pipelines, is Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh is around INR1,432 crores. We have spent around INR150 crores. By the end of this year, we will be spending around INR450 crores. Next year, we are looking at spending around INR600 crores, and subsequent

items.statement: Mumbai BKC project capex remains INR 800 crores (INR 400 crores equity, INR 400 crores debt).
items.quote: There is no change in the overall capex cost as of now. The INR 800 crores of our committed capex remains the same; INR 400 crores of equity and INR 400 crores of debt.

items.statement: Contracted over 5,200 keys by FY30, with ~2,600 owned keys, roughly 50-50 split.
items.quote: Our goal currently, we are already contracted, and at various, including our openings that we are at various stages of development, at over 5,200 keys by FY30, and which will include 2,600 or so keys, which will be under our ownership.

items.statement: Pitching for mid-to-high double-digit corporate rate growth for CY27.
items.quote: So we are pitching for mid-to-high double-digit growth rates in terms of our ask rates, but the negotiations are on.

items.statement: Expects strong H2 with domestic leisure and destination demand continuing to grow.
items.quote: This year, because of the global situation, we expect that the internal domestic business will also continue to grow, especially on the leisure and destination side. So we expect a very strong closing for the year

items.statement: Suite occupancy rose over 700 bps, with paid suite occupancy in mid-40s.
items.quote: If you look at our portfolio, our suite occupancy has risen by over 700 basis points.

items.statement: Dubai JV hotel operating at breakeven EBITDA; ADRs lagging due to low international demand.
items.quote: The hotel was operationally breakeven even in Q2, and the on-the-ground situation has not got fully resolved, but there was an improvement in occupancy, and the ADR level was low because international demand is not there.

items.statement: Will seek shareholder approval for investment in BKC JV to buy entire FSI.
items.quote: Since this is a material transaction with a related party, with the JV entity, Leela will shortly reach out to the shareholders for an approval of investment.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected in 20s for FY27.
items.quote: We anticipate an effective tax rate to be in 20s in FY27.

items.statement: Borrowing costs reduced by 30 bps from mid-October after lender renegotiation.
items.quote: Additionally, our borrowing costs have reduced by a further 30 basis points from mid-October, as we have actively renegotiated with our lenders, which provides a shield from potential transmission of policy rate hikes.
